ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a neural pathway: a signal begins at sensory endings in the skin, travels along a neuron with an axon and cell body, connects through terminal/synaptic regions to another neuron, and then continues to a motor ending at a muscle. Reasoning: In such neural pathways, adjacent neurons or target cells are separated by synapses or terminal junctions. Neurotransmitters such as acetylcholine are the chemical messengers released at these junctions to pass the signal onward. Their effect is to change the activity of the postsynaptic cell, either exciting it or inhibiting it.
